title: Cumulative Counts of Maximal Induced Bicliques in the Random Graph Process
content: We study maximal induced bicliques along a uniformly random ordering of the edges of \( K_n \). For every fixed \( r\ge1 \), both the number of distinct bicliques with smaller side of size \( r \) and their number of births are \( \exp(\Theta(n^{1/(r+1)})) \) with high probability; consequently, asymptotically almost all births are bicliques with a singleton side (stars). We determine the exact exponential rate of the expected counts, prove a strict exponential gap between expectation and typical behavior, and obtain the first two terms of the typical logarithmic counts in the successive limits \( n\to\infty \) and \( r\to\infty \). The common-neighborhood reduction leads to the entropy of maximal independent sets in sparse random graphs. Using a three-state tree recursion and a renewal estimate for boundary influence, we prove that this entropy exists up to mean degree \( 42/25 \), which yields an exact typical rate for bicliques with a prescribed smaller side in a sparse random-graph snapshot, within the same range. In contrast with the worst-case cumulative bound \( \Theta(n3^{n/3}) \), the random filtration admits \( \exp(O(\sqrt n)) \) total-time change-sensitive enumeration, with high probability and in expectation.
